newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tass agency says Pol Pot story fake.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tass agency says Pol Pot story fake.

text.p: The Russian news agency Itar-Tass said on Tuesday it had nothing to do with a website which had reported Khmer Rouge guerrilla leader Pol Pot was in Sweden seeking political asylum, and said the story was fake anyway.

The story, which appeared on a website whose Internet address is www.tass.net, said Pol Pot had arrived at Arlanda airport on Monday afternoon and was picked up by members of a left-wing group in Stockholm.
"Itar-Tass news agency has nothing to do with this website which obviously is a pirate one," said Boris Polosyants, the chief coordinator of the agency's Internet projects.
"We have several web sites but definitely not this one," he told Reuters. The key Itar-Tass web site has the Internet address www.itar-tass.com.
Itar-Tass deputy director Pavel Mikhalev told Reuters the agency had never issued such a story.
"It must be a pirate act," he said. "We have not run this story."

Pol Pot -- the man held responsible for the death of more than one million Cambodians during his 1975-79 "Killing Fields" rule -- has not been seen in public since late 1979 and his whereabouts are not definitely known.
There have been recent reports that he was captured by his own former Khmer Rouge supporters in Cambodia.
Mikhalev said the first the agency's correspondent in Sweden knew about the Pol Pot story on the Internet was when the Swedish Foreign Ministry asked him about it.
The website which published the Pol Pot story describes itself as a homepage of the Tass.Net organisation but gives no other information about who runs it.
